quote:
The main selling point of this trilogy is the art style AC Chronicles China uses one inspired by Chinese ink and brush paintings and I think it is the game that nails the art style it was going for the best AC Chronicles India's art style is inspired by Mughal art and architecture and it does look pretty at times unfortunately that one was also the most broken of the trilogy while AC Chronicles Russia uses an art style inspired by Soviet era propoganda and this one does the worst of actually utilizing and recreating the art style

Of the stories AC Chronicles India is probably the best AC Chronicles China is the second best and Russia is the worst

Gameplay-wise, I think Russia is the best one because it is the most unique, letting you play two different characters, one of which has no way to attack outside of stealth assassinations, adding more challenge to certain sections. AC Chronicles India and China are basically the same, with the main difference being that things you had to unlock in AC Chronicles China are already unlocked in AC Chronicles India, making the gameplay more fluid feeling

quote:
This could have genuinely been an amazing game and it started out pretty good but there are so many problems that I had with it as I progressed through the game but there are 3 major problems 

The first major problem is that the exploration is just awful and feeling unrewarding with most of the puzzles being uninteresting or being the same puzzle, and at times you need to get to a certain area out of reach but its incredibly hard to find how to get to them because you need to do a specific thing to get to the area but the devs made it really hard to find what you need to do because the devs wanted to encourage exploration

The second major problem is the Titan bosses they are just unfun to fight compared to the mini-bosses in the open world since you can't take damage as Super Sonic and it is decided by how many rings you had when you entered the fight, near the end of their fights the game tells you to mash X on Xbox but if you do what the game is telling you to do its almost impossible actually beat the boss and you will almost certainly die so what you actually have to do is move the joysticks in a circle meaning the game is literally giving you wrong instructions on what to do

quote:
I think this could have been one of the better Silent Hill games and I liked a lot of the ideas the devs had for this game but I feel like they were not utilized to their fullest extent or were just given up on halfway if even halfway, I liked how they leaned into the more mazelike structure of Silent Hill but when you did reach your objective it wasn't always clear that you did since every now and then it blended into the environment, I liked how they put a bigger focus on the side missions but not how they were handled, I liked the bigger focus on exploration compared to other Silent Hill games but the fact the game barely gives you any hint in any way on how to get to your objectives can be frustrating, and I liked the more cinematic approach the game had in the beginning but I felt like when you reached Silent Hill they didn't utilize it enough, and there are more things I liked the idea of but the game either didn't fully utilize it or it felt like the game gave up on the idea early on


but the reason this game is a 6 and not a 7 or an 8 is solely because of the combat its genuinely one of the most frustrating things in any Silent Hill game (and that says a lot because Silent Hill games are always extremely janky in some way) and its not due to any one specific reason the weapons break and that could have been fine but they also have super weak durability and the fights are almost always in groups, the most common enemy has a ranged stun attack they will also often spawn right behind you and they never stops chasing you unless you run into a building which are usually large distances apart from each other and they are often grouped together in groups of 3 enemies and because of this you can't just run from fights like in previous Silent Hill games because you just get constantly stunned and then attacked by a different enemy and to make it worst the combat was not designed for group combat due to the fact that the lock on cant be switched (I tried every button to try and switch the lock on target it never did so if there is a lock on switch it didnt work for me) and the fact that the lock on would never lock on to the target I wanted it to but would always go to the exact enemy I didn't want to attack at that time and I learned early on that if you don't finish an enemy when they fall down they will just get back up and attack you while you fight the other enemies but while you do this the other enemies will repeatedly just attack you and to make matters worst apparently if you finish them when they are down this which will give you negative karma which affects the ending you get and most of the time from my experience the enemies get backup when they are knocked down and there are more ways that this games combat gets more and more frustrating as the game goes on

author: BleedingJester
quote:
Im gonna start this off with the positives this is a fun game and compared to a lot of JRPGs especially older ones the grinding isnt bad partially since the leveling system is split between the character's level and the class level both using two different types of exp with the Class level being far more important and once you know the right way to grind your class it takes something that could have taken days and turns it into hours making this a decent game to start playing JRPGs with (as long as you have a glass guide), the art style of the game will look familiar to Dragon Ball and Dragon Quest fans since Akira Toriyama and while I wont spoil the Story it's also pretty good and works very well with the art style, it also works very well and I truly hope this gets ported to PC at some point so more people can play this great game


now for the bad 
I think the sound design is the worst part of the game a lot of the music is just generic JRPG music and would work fine in most JRPGs but the Boss music is truly awful there is a single song that is used on repeat every boss fight and while you are probably thinking that doesn't sound bad well in some areas you will end up fighting a boss every minute and the boss fights can drag on and if you lose the fight you'll go to a nearby checkpoint and will basically immediately fight the boss and hear the music again this alone is why I rated this game a 6it got so bad that I literally had to take off my headphones so I couldn't hear it cause I was getting a migraine, the next issue is the difficulty spikes it felt random in a lot of ways with some areas being super hard and compared to the previous areas it honestly just ruined the pacing of the game, the last negative I want to point out is the animations they are good but some of them take roughly a minute and yeah a Minute isn't long by itself but that adds up so you'll end up fighting the same opponent twenty time well that's roughly twenty minutes of you watching the same animation repeatedly with no way of skipping which made me partially hate the combat which while not anything unique in the JRPG genre it was still fun at first anyway but after I got tired of seeing the same animation play repeatedly for the enemies I just started to avoid combat in general which made me under leveled near the end of the game, there are mechanics that get very little explanation and these aren't minor mechanics that don't mean anything these are the class mechanics which affects how you grind, how you use certain characters in combat, and if you'll even be able to progress after a certain point in the game and honestly the way it's explained made it seem like it's not important but it's very important in fact its so important its basically the core of the game


I do think this game is worth playing if you are a fan of JRPGs and have never played it before or want to get into JRPG games and its definitely one of the best Xbox Exclusives even now and its definitely a great JRPG in general but you should look at a guide so you don't end up having to go back roughly 6 hours of playtime and then spend roughly 5 hours grinding so you can go

author: BleedingJester
quote:
The story is pretty good in both Cyber Sleuth and Hackers Memory and they are almost completely separate stories that interconnect at specific points you should play both to get the full story of both games I suggest you start with Cyber Sleuth and move onto Hackers Memory

Gameplay this is a turn based JRPG and I don't you start with this game if your new to the genre but if you like Pokémon and want something more challenging this would be a good choice as you can evolve and devolve and there is a rock, paper, scissors style of combat kind of like Pokémon but the game doesn't properly explain some things such as how to equip equipment or that you can teleport back to the entrance of a dungeon you will also repeatedly revisit certain locations sometimes in the same chapter which makes them really repetitive

Characters I found some of the characters really annoying in the game in Cyber Sleuth it was Nokia and in the beginning of Hackers Memory it was Wormmon but for the most part I did like characters especially in Hackers Memory

overall I highly suggest this game if you either love Digimon and want to get into the games or you love JRPGs and are looking for a new one to play but this isnt a game for beginners to the genre

there were a few bugs but if you just restart to the last checkpoint then they wont really have game breaking effects from what I experienced
